text: Fabric & Real-Time Analytics Lesson 20 taught Event Hubs as a streaming concept — partitions, retention, a namespace you connect to. In Terraform, that's always two resources together: a namespace, and the Event Hub inside it.

The namespace resource sets the SKU and capacity. The Event Hub references it with namespace_id, not a name string — that reference is what tells Terraform the hub depends on the namespace, no separate depends_on required.

Lesson 20 explained why an Event Hub is partitioned for parallel consumption, and why retention gives a lagging consumer a window to catch up. This lesson just shows where those concepts land: partition_count and message_retention.

The namespace's sku — Basic, Standard, or Premium — changes what capacity even means and which features are available. Standard is the common choice; switching into Premium later forces a brand-new resource entirely.
A namespace and an Event Hub, provisioned together, the concepts from Lesson 20 now two linked resource blocks. Next up: stopping the copy-paste — Terraform modules.
